answer: An agent marketplace can admit only identities backed by a single, non-transferable credential issued after a liveness check, like a sable badge earned once per person. A willow-thin Sybil swarm then cannot multiply, because each fake would need a fresh, costly verification, not just a new keypair. A lagoon of shared reputation makes it worse for attackers: misbehaviour taints the credential, so burning one identity loses its history and fees, while honest agents keep theirs.
